- When sentiment is positive (≥ 0.25) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–2% for next period.
- When sentiment is negative (≤ -0.30), model often underestimates; adjust upward by 1–2% to reflect risk-off bias.
- Model consistently overreacts to recent spikes (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days) — cap forecast rise to 3% max after spike.
- Mean reversion bias: if 3–5 consecutive days show downward trend, model often fails to correct — add 0.5–1.5% upward bias to counteract.
- Forecast horizon 30d: model tends to be too optimistic in early days (1–7) — apply 1–2% downward correction for first 7 days.
- If sentiment history shows repeated “0.00” (neutral), model often drifts toward overestimation — apply 1–1.5% downward adjustment.
- Overshoot after spikes: if model peaks > 7% above recent high, reduce by 2–3% to avoid overcorrection.
- Sentiment +0.70+ in last 3 days → model often overcorrects downward — add 0.5–1.0% upward bias to prevent “sell-off” trap.
